ops.title: EDEADLK reading FP-synth settings.json — likely double-materialization race
ops.body:
**Incident**: Claude Code (acct-13, Yasyf-9) hit `EDEADLK: unknown error, read` reading `/Users/yasyf/.cc-pool/accounts/acct-13/settings.json` (FP-backed). Transient — same file read fine moments later.

**Path confirmed**: settings.json is a synth/"computed" entry (`content.EntrySynth`, internal/overlay/contentsource.go:76), not a passthrough symlink. Reads go: `FileProviderExtension.fetchContents` (widget/Sources/FileProvider/FileProviderExtension.swift:292-332) → `BridgeClient.readSynth` (widget/Sources/FileProvider/BridgeClient.swift:77-80, fresh AF_UNIX conn per call to the group-container `b.sock`) → daemon's `content.BridgeServer.handleRead` (fusekit@v1.0.1 content/bridge.go:306-316) → `PoolContentSource.ReadSynth` (internal/overlay/contentsource.go:124-135, lock-free local `os.ReadFile`).

**Ruled out**: exhaustive case-insensitive search for "EDEADLK"/"deadlock" — zero hits in cc-pool, one unrelated hit in fusekit (mountd/server.go:734, mux-mount claim protocol, not reachable from FP). No daemon-side lock is held across the settings.json read path. The bridge wire protocol (fusekit content/bridge.go) carries only string errors + an ErrClass enum — no mechanism exists for a raw POSIX errno to cross the daemon↔appex socket. Neither BridgeClient.swift nor FileProviderExtension.swift ever constructs a POSIXError; `mapUnreachable` (FileProviderExtension.swift:643-651) only ever produces `NSFileProviderError.serverUnreachable`. No `evictItem` call exists anywhere in the codebase (only `signalEnumerator(for: .workingSet)`, which just bumps the sync anchor).

**Leading hypothesis (unproven, best fit to all observed facts)**: `item(for:)` (metadata/getattr, FileProviderExtension.swift:281-290) and `fetchContents` (content read, :292-332) are both dispatched via `queue.async` onto the SAME concurrent `DispatchQueue` (:75-76) with zero per-item serialization on either the Swift or Go side — `BridgeClient.roundTrip` opens a fresh socket per call, the daemon spawns a fresh goroutine per connection, nothing coalesces two requests for the same item. A stat/getattr (`computedItem`→`synthSize`, :167-183, a full `bridge.readSynth` just for byte count) and an open+read for the SAME not-yet-materialized computed item can therefore race through fileproviderd concurrently. fileproviderd's own per-item replica-coordination lock (closed-source, standard NSFileProviderReplicatedExtension internals) is the plausible source of the EDEADLK fast-fail — matches transient + resolves-on-retry + no reachable code path in cc-pool/fusekit.

**Proposed fix (not yet implemented)**: add per-item request coalescing in FileProviderExtension.swift — an in-flight-request gate keyed by `itemIdentifier.rawValue` that serializes `item(for:)` and `fetchContents` for the same id (both ops are idempotent reads, so the second caller can just wait and reuse). Complementary: extend `SynthSizeCache` (or add a sibling) to cache the actual synth bytes by content-version, not just the size, so a `fetchContents` immediately following a `computedItem`/`synthSize` call for the same version skips the second bridge round trip entirely — this is the most common trigger shape (stat-then-read).

fusekit pinned at v1.0.1 (current latest); no upstream fix for this exists yet.
